mathematicalReview.reason: From exit speed x to next entry upper bound y,the shortest connector has length max(x-y,0),leaves min(x,y)>=1,and is accepted. Every original entry accepts the initial1. No final return term belongs to the objective.

Set U=max of both entries and exits. Adding required U->1 after the original last section and before the first costs0 at both joins. An abstract free x->y with x<=y records acceptance by a larger upper limit,not physical acceleration. Conversely,cut any augmented Euler cycle after the auxiliary and retain original required arcs in order;total downward variation of a connector path from x to y is at least max(x-y,0). Replacing it by a direct legal slowdown and dropping auxiliary-adjacent joins cannot increase cost. These two inequalities make the optima equal.

Every connector between endpoint speeds expands monotonically along consecutive compressed coordinates with exactly the same downward length and zero upward cost. Intermediate vertices may be visited but required arcs are still taken whole. A mandatory long arc joins its two endpoints only for weak connectivity; it does not automatically join all intermediate speeds.

mathematicalReview.reason: For each cut,closed traversal requires added downward minus upward count equal the mandatory right-minus-left crossing count b. Thus every solution has d=max(b,0)+z,u=max(-b,0)+z,integer z>=0. Base cost sum max(b,0)*gap is unavoidable. Zero net cut balances imply each individual vertex degree balance by adjacent prefix subtraction,total mandatory degree difference being0.

Required endpoints and every nonzero-b minimum correction already connect their boundary endpoints in the base graph. An additional opposite pair on such a cut cannot merge distinct base components. Only zero-b gaps can merge components,and every connected solution must supply a connected set of these quotient edges. Each chosen pair pays its gap;with nonnegative costs it contains a spanning tree costing at least the minimum spanning tree.

Add a pair of opposite adjacent connectors for every Kruskal-selected zero cut. Degree equality is unchanged and all base components join. Candidate edges together with already connected gaps cover the full coordinate line,so spanning is possible. A weakly connected directed multigraph balanced at every nonzero-degree vertex has an Euler circuit:otherwise its SCC condensation would have a nontrivial source with positive net outflow,contradicting balance. This achieves the lower bound and maps back to a feasible physical ordering.

Repeated sections are separate required arcs and contribute multiplicity to delta. Equal s=t gives a loop,zero local delta and an active endpoint component that may still require connection. With all speeds1 there is one vertex,no gaps,and answer0. Including maximal exits in U is necessary;using only entries is not the implemented method.
